description: **Files selfdoc rewrites keep their permissions.** A file selfdoc wrote without a declared mode (the docs-state manifests, the content hash and revision records, the derived ignore file, posts the blog editor saves, the assembly's generated pages) came back readable by its owner alone (0600). An existing file now keeps its mode, and a new one gets 0644 as modified by the umask.

**A refused `.strictcli/schema.json` names the command that regenerates it.** A schema on the wrong `schema_version`, or with no `project_id`, was refused naming `<app> --dump-schema`, which current strictcli refuses; the refusal now names `<app> help --json > .strictcli/schema.json`, and the first strictcli of each implementation that has `help --json` (Go 0.37.0, Python 0.44.0, TypeScript 0.43.0).

**`table-commands` lists nested command groups.** A group declared inside another group (`apple testers`, say) and its subcommands were missing from the table; every group at any depth now gets its heading row and every command its row, each under its full path (`apple testers remove`).

**CLI reference pages document nested command groups.** A group declared inside another group (`apple testers`, say) and its subcommands were left off the generated pages; each nested group now gets a section on its top-level group's page, at any depth, followed by a section for each of its commands under its full path (`apple testers remove`).

**`selfdoc check` covers nested command groups.** `cli-help-text-too-short` now measures the help of groups nested inside other groups and of their commands, flags, and arguments, and `undocumented-cli-command-or-flag` now requires the flags of those commands to appear on the top-level group's page; both had looked only one level deep.

**The strictcli schema is read from `.strictmetadata/.cli-schema/schema.json`.** CLI reference pages, `table-commands`, and `selfdoc check` read a project's `help --json` document there; `.strictcli/schema.json` is no longer read. Every refusal that says how to regenerate the schema now prints `mkdir -p .strictmetadata/.cli-schema && <app> help --json > .strictmetadata/.cli-schema/schema.json`, which runs as shown in a project that has no `.strictmetadata/` yet. Move an existing schema with `selfdoc layout migrate`.

**Each uncommitted directory carries its own ignore file.** `.strictmetadata/` now holds directories only, with `go.mod` as the one file beside them: selfdoc writes `.strictmetadata/.docs-cache/.gitignore` instead of a block in `.strictmetadata/.gitignore`, and `selfdoc layout validate` reports a `.strictmetadata/.gitignore` with the command that converts it and no longer reports `.strictmetadata/go.mod`. `selfdoc layout dump` names each directory's `ignore_path` and `ignore_content` and the `root_files`, in place of the one `ignore_file`. Convert a repository with `selfdoc layout migrate` (run `--dry-run` first).

**`selfdoc layout migrate` moves strictcli's files under `.strictmetadata/`.** Every `.strictcli/` directory's committed `schema.json` moves to `.strictmetadata/.cli-schema/schema.json`, its `test-coverage.json` to `.strictmetadata/.cli-test-coverage/manifest.json`, and its coverage shards to `.strictmetadata/.cli-test-coverage/shards/`, with a `manifest.toml` naming `strictcli` in each directory and the `.gitignore` that keeps the shards out of the repository. The stub `go.mod`, rlsbl's scaffold base of it and its `.rlsbl/managed-files.json` entry, the root `.gitignore`'s `coverage/` line, and the emptied directories go. A file the move cannot place, one git does not track, or a taken destination is refused by name. `selfdoc layout validate` accepts directories owned by `strictcli` without a `strictcli` executable on `PATH`.

**Every `root_files` entry names its template and every file it generates: `{"template": ".strictmetadata/docs/_README.md", "outputs": ["README.md", "pypi/README.md"]}`.** One template can now generate several files, such as a package directory's own README kept in step with the root one. A plain template string is refused with an error naming the migration: run `selfdoc layout migrate --dry-run`, then `selfdoc layout migrate`, which converts every entry to the output selfdoc generated from it. `gen` writes every declared output and refuses a hand-written or git-ignored one before writing any, and `check` reads every output for the version check.
